mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 0.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative in periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) combined with elevated interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 0.5%) signals a dual stress on the economy, compressing corporate profits and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in triggered instances (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) and rising interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 0.5%), the Federal Reserve's tightening policy compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in late-cycle expansion periods (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust economic activity and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate above 5.0% signals a weakening labor market and reduced consumer spending, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) is above 5.0% and non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) are below 145,000 thousand, the combined signal indicates a deteriorating labor market with weak job creation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in triggered instances (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer confidence and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
